metadata.indicator_name: Rate of growth of Total Annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at constant prices
metadata.definition:
The growth rate of annual total gross domestic product (GDP) at constant prices measures the percentage change in the volume of GDP between one year and the previous year. By using values at constant 2018 prices, the indicator reflects changes in the level of GDP, excluding the effect of price changes.

Regional and subregional totals are based on available data for the countries of the region.
metadata.calculation_methodology:
To compile national accounts series for the region at constant 2018 prices, ECLAC uses current GDP values for 2018 as the reference and retropolates and extrapolates them using the corresponding volume indices obtained from each country’s official national accounts series. This procedure makes it possible to construct harmonized series at constant 2018 prices while preserving the volume growth rates officially reported by each country.

As a result of the retropolation and extrapolation process, differences may arise in GDP levels relative to national series expressed using their own reference years. However, these differences do not affect growth rates, since the methodology preserves the year-on-year volume changes reported in each country’s official series.

The annual growth rate for year is calculated as follows:

Growth ratet=((GDPt/1GDPt-1)−1)×100

where GDPt corresponds to GDP at constant prices in year, GDPt-1 and to GDP in the immediately preceding year.

For regional and subregional aggregates, the growth rate is calculated from the change in the aggregate levels of GDP at constant prices for countries with available information in both years considered.
